evidence.quote: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

Acts.23.5->Acts.24.17.limitations: Broad narrative association only unless the editorial intent is supplied.

2Cor.4.18->Lev.16.25-Lev.16.26.relation: Eternal unseen things versus ritual burning and washing
2Cor.4.18->Lev.16.25-Lev.16.26.reason: Corinthians contrasts temporary affliction/visible things with eternal glory. The selected Leviticus verses prescribe burning fat and washing after releasing the scapegoat. No specific visible/unseen or temporal/eternal claim appears in that range.

evidence.quote: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen [are] temporal; but the things which are not seen [are] eternal.
And the fat of the sin offering shall he burn upon the altar.
And he that let go the goat for the scapegoat shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward come into the camp.

2Cor.4.18->Lev.16.25-Lev.16.26.limitations: An asserted typology would need evidence beyond this bare connection.

Heb.3.4->Esth.3.9.relation: God as builder versus Haman's proposal to destroy Jews
Heb.3.4->Esth.3.9.reason: Hebrews compares the honour of Christ and Moses using the builder/house illustration. Esther records Haman offering money for destruction of a people. The target does not support divine creation or the builder analogy.

evidence.quote: For every house is builded by some [man;] but he that built all things [is] God.

If it please the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring [it] into the king's treasuries.

Heb.3.4->Esth.3.9.limitations: No contradiction between the biblical passages is implied by this unsupported editorial link.
